bio: My research focuses on dynamic decision making under uncertainty, leveraging tools from applied probability, queueing theory, mathematical optimization, and statistics. I formulate operational problems such as stochastic network models and design scalable algorithms to compute near-optimal policies, including the use of reinforcement learning and neural-network approaches to solve high-dimensional control problems. I'm especially interested in settings that couple learning from data with operations management. Applications include dynamic pricing, inventory control, production scheduling, supply chain management, and human AI interactions.

department: Department of Mathematical and Statistical Sciences
bio: My research interests include random networks and extreme value theory. I am interested in designing scalable models that capture the salient features of real-world network data such as heavy-tailed degree distributions and temporal shifts in connection dynamics. I typically gear my work towards modeling social media user interactions (e.g. Facebook, Reddit), though it may also be applied to other types of network data (e.g. World Wide Web, protein-protein interaction networks). Since network models usually employ latent variables to describe complex interaction phenomena, I employ standard data science tools in my work, such as Bayesian statistics and EM algorithms.
